cards.explanation: The answer is the house of Israel and the royal house. The LORD says, “Hear this, O priests! Take heed, O house of Israel! Give ear, O royal house!” That's three groups called by name. Nobody gets to say it was meant for the person standing next to them.

The answer is a net spread out. The LORD says they have been “…a snare at Mizpah, a net spread out on Tabor.” Mizpah and Tabor are the two places He names. A snare and a net are both made to catch someone, and nobody spreads one out as a welcome mat.

The answer is False. The LORD says the rebels are deep in slaughter, “but I will chastise them all.” Not just the worst of them, friends, all of them. This is a heavy verse, and I think it's meant to be taken seriously.
The answer is defiled. The LORD says, “I know all about Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from Me.” Then He says, “Israel is defiled.” He isn't guessing here. He knows all about it.

The answer is False. Hosea 5:4 says a spirit of prostitution is within them, “…and they do not know the LORD.” It also says their deeds do not permit them to return to their God. So this is about people who don't know Him, not people who still do.

The answer is False. Judah does not keep its footing. The verse says, “even Judah stumbles with them.” Judah followed the house of David (1 Kings 12:20), and it still stumbles here. When you see the word “even,” brace yourselves.

The answer is that they don't find Him. They go with their flocks and herds to seek the LORD, “…but they do not find Him…” The verse adds that “He has withdrawn Himself from them.” That stings, friends.

The answer is that He has withdrawn Himself from them. They seek Him and don't find Him, because “He has withdrawn Himself from them.” This is a sobering verse. The LORD doesn't leave it as a mystery, either. He tells us right there that He withdrew.
The answer is True, and it's both. The verse says, “Now the New Moon will devour them along with their land.” Not just the people, the land too. That's a lot to take in, so I'll just say it plainly.
The answer is a battle cry. The verse says, “raise the battle cry in Beth-aven…” The ram's horn goes in Gibeah and the trumpet in Ramah. Horn, trumpet and battle cry make a loud list.
The answer is True. The verse says, “Ephraim will be laid waste on the day of rebuke.” Then the LORD adds, “Among the tribes of Israel I proclaim what is certain.” He doesn't say maybe.

The answer is water. The LORD says, “I will pour out My fury upon them like water.” Water pours and spreads out and doesn't stop at the edge of the table. That's a lot of fury, and I'll leave it right there.

The answer is that he is determined to follow worthless idols. The verse says Ephraim is “…oppressed, crushed in judgment, for he is determined to follow worthless idols.” The text gives the reason right there. Determined is a strong word, too.
The answer is decay. The LORD says, “So I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like decay to the house of Judah.” A moth and decay aren't a thunderclap. They're the slow kind of trouble.

The answer is Assyria. The verse says, “…then Ephraim turned to Assyria and sent to the great king.” Assyria is the nation Ephraim looks to for help. The LORD then says that king “…cannot cure you or heal your wound.”
The answer is False. Ephraim sends to the great king, but the LORD says, “But he cannot cure you or heal your wound.” The king can't do either one. Ephraim sent to the wrong place for a cure.

The answer is that He will go away and carry them off. The LORD says, “I, even I, will tear them to pieces and then go away. I will carry them off where no one can rescue them.” That's a heavy verse, and I think it's okay to feel that. I'll just let the verse say it.
The answer is False. The LORD says, “I will carry them off where no one can rescue them.” So nobody is going to step in and rescue Ephraim and Judah. It's a heavy ending to the lion picture.

The answers are guilt and face. The LORD says He will return to His place “…until they admit their guilt and seek My face…” Admitting guilt is hard, and I've had to say a few things out loud myself. And He doesn't say seek My gifts or My help, friends, He says seek My face. Faces are for looking at the one you want to see.

The answer is that He will heal us and bind up our wounds. The call says, “For He has torn us to pieces, but He will heal us; He has wounded us, but He will bind up our wounds.” The word “but” is doing a lot of work in that sentence. I like where that word takes us.
The answer is True. The call says, “After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up…” Revive first, then raise up. It's a two-step, and both steps are His.

The answer is that we may live in His presence. The call says, “on the third day He will raise us up, that we may live in His presence.” The point is to be with Him. That's about the best reason I can think of.
The answer is that it is certain to happen. The call says, “As surely as the sun rises, He will appear…” The sun rising is the picture of something you can count on. So His appearing is just as sure.

The answer is rain. The call says, “He will come to us like the rain, like the spring showers that water the earth.” Rain is something the earth is glad to see. It's a gentle ending after a rough passage.
